Destination calendars without a credentialId can no longer match in Google createEvent, so events go to the 'primary' calendar instead of the configured externalId, which is a behavioral regression.
Letting any attendee add arbitrary guests, who then receive invites sent in the organizer's name, is a concrete authorization and abuse risk, not a minor point.

The template string is always truthy, so the fallback never runs and users can see a malformed error toast such as "undefined: ...", which is a concrete incorrect behavior.
Reminders with a missing sendTo or empty message never get retryCount incremented, so they are retried on every cron run, which defeats the purpose of the PR.
The default export has the wrong function name (`TwoFactor` instead of `BackupCode`). This is a naming/readability issue with no functional impact, since the import name is what callers use.

Outside controllers, fallback locales are never loaded, so keys missing in the current locale return 'translation missing' and that wrong result gets cached.
The unescaped request.referer inside an inline JS string can be broken out of with a quote in the path on the allowed host, since only the host is validated, which is a concrete XSS.

An unescaped url in raw_html content rendered via `raw` allows HTML/attribute injection (XSS), since the only validation is an http(s) prefix check.
A feed item with no content (only a description) makes `i.content.scrub` raise NoMethodError on nil, which aborts the poll so later items are never imported.
